in: Create ONE new Java package, com.securityexpert.nexus.ui2.discovery.pan, inside the EXISTING ui2/platform-core module. No new Gradle subproject, no new dependency.

The one candidate shape, section 4 and sections 5 to 9: a raw input record and a candidate row carrying, by ROLE name, the stable identifier (serial, Optional -- ID-2/U-1), the display name, the device-type marker carried as-is even when empty (CL-3), the two address roles as SEPARATE Optional fields for the IPv4 locator and the IPv6 locator (ID-4), the peer-serial reference (Optional, HA-0), the connection-state element (Optional, LV-0), the connection timestamp element and the certificate elements (Optional, CS-1/CS-2, each under its own name), and the nested virtual-system entries (VS-1) each with its own identifier, display name and the three shared-policy elements under three role names (VS-2). No kind lattice and no computed kind (CL-1, CL-3). Every '?'-shaped field is Optional and its absence is handled, never repaired.

Identity, section 5: the serial is opaque -- not cast, not trimmed of leading zeroes, not normalized, not parsed (ID-1). Representation-equality for the join is decided after trimming SURROUNDING whitespace only (check 11 fixes exactly that) and after nothing else. The display name is never compared (ID-3). Neither address is ever compared to form any relationship (ID-4/ID-5) -- host resolution and pairing are written with no access to either address field; make that structural (the resolver signatures do not receive addresses).

Virtual systems, section 6: each nested entry becomes a candidate row in its own right (VS-4) whose host link is exactly its parent entry, read off the structure with zero lookups (VS-3); the virtual-system identifier is scoped to its parent (VS-2). Do not build a two-address host invariant -- the contract says that problem does not exist here.

High availability, section 7: a PairingOutcome type with PAIRED and NOT_EVALUABLE, the latter carrying WHY as a closed enum (no serial; peer resolves to no entry HA-2; peer names self HA-3; one-sided HA-4). A pair forms only when A names B and B names A within the same input set (HA-1). HA-4a: an inbound claim on a member of a reciprocal pair leaves that pair PAIRED. HA-4b: that member additionally carries the unreciprocated inbound claim(s), by the claimant's serial, as a separate outcome field -- surfaced, never resolved into a pair, never dropped. HA-5: every candidate is returned with its outcome.

Sections 8 and 9: no field name and no enumerated value in the package uses up/down/online/offline/reachable/unreachable/healthy/unhealthy or a synonym; no value is derived from the connection-state, connection-timestamp or certificate elements (LV-1 to LV-3, CS-1/CS-2); they are carried under their own names only.

Section 10: the assembler returns exactly one row per input entry plus one per nested virtual-system entry; nothing is dropped for a missing serial (DI-4), for a non-established or absent connection state (DI-5), or for any NOT_EVALUABLE outcome (DI-6). No deduplication (DI-7).

One isolated field-binding site: a PanoramaApiFieldBinding class mirroring cp's ManagementApiFieldBinding -- one Role enum covering every role above, one entry per role naming a CANDIDATE response element path, every entry UNVERIFIED (section 11 check 14 is what would verify them, and it needs a live Panorama this movement does not have); a role you cannot even propose an element for is UNKNOWN and not carried. Every rule in the package is written against Role names; no other production class contains a concrete element name.

JUnit tests implementing section 11 Band 2 checks 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 over synthetic fixtures constructed in the test source (no real serial, name, address or estate value -- follow cp's Fixtures.java discipline). Check 7 MUST assert all five cases explicitly and separately, and the fifth case must assert both that the B-C pair stays PAIRED and that B carries A's inbound claim. Check 8 replaces every device and virtual-system display name with one constant and asserts identical pairing outcomes and host links. Check 9 asserts the vocabulary rule over every field name and every enum constant name in the package, and that no field is a function of the connection-state element. Check 10 gives two candidates identical IPv4 and IPv6 values and asserts no relationship forms. Check 11 asserts whitespace-padded serials pair identically and a removed serial yields NOT_EVALUABLE with no name- or address-based fallback. Check 12 asserts each virtual-system row's host link is its parent with zero simulated calls.
Commit early and often on the lane, grouped by contract section (shape and binding; identity and virtual systems; HA pairing; sections 8 to 10; Band 2 tests).
